Functional Description: Computes the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of a matrix using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). It decomposes the input matrix A into its singular value components, inverts the non-zero singular values above a certain threshold to avoid numerical instability, and reconstructs the pseudoinverse using these components. Supports input of float, double, cfloat, and cdouble dtypes, and can handle batches of matrices.
Wrapper Entry Information: def pseudoinverse_svd(A, *, full_matrices=True, rcond=1e-15, out=None) -> Tensor

Args:
    A (Tensor): Input tensor of shape `(*, m, n)` where `*` is zero or more batch dimensions.

Keyword args:
    full_matrices (bool, optional): If `True` (default), compute the full SVD. If `False`, compute the reduced SVD.
    rcond (float, optional): Relative condition number threshold. Singular values smaller than `rcond * largest_singular_value` are set to zero. Default: `1e-15`.
    out (Tensor, optional): Output tensor. Ignored if `None`. Default: `None`.
Math: A^{+} = V^{\mathrm{H}} \Sigma^{+} U^{\mathrm{H}}; \sigma_i^{+} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{\sigma_i}, & \text{if } \sigma_i > \text{rcond} \times \sigma_{\max} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
